items.text: Nearly nine in ten of its members cosponsored from its introduction a bill giving people brought to the country as children, and holders of temporary protection from removal, permanent residence and a path to citizenship. An independent estimate of an identical earlier version put those potentially eligible at up to about 4.4 million people, about 1.3 percent of the population.

Its working group on immigration proposed a plan that would fund at least 22,000 border agents and more border technology, add 100,000 permanent residence visas a year for graduates of the country's colleges and lift country caps on work visas, give people brought to the country as children a path to citizenship, and give adults without legal status who have lived in the country five years, have no felony record and work or study a temporary legal status that can lead to permanent residence.
